parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Nitrogen dioxide emissions can be reduced by adding an aqueous solution of urea, (NH 2 ) 2 CO, to car exhaust gases. The heat of the exhaust gases breaks down the urea into simpler substances.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) One molecule of urea breaks down to form one molecule of ammonia and one other molecule. Complete the chemical equation to show the formula of the other molecule formed in this reaction. (NH 2 ) 2 CO → NH 3 + ...................... [1]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) The ammonia formed reacts with nitrogen dioxide to form nitrogen and water.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Balance the equation for this reaction. ..........NO 2 + ..........NH 3 → ..........N 2 + 12H 2 O [2]

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) 135 moles of urea, (NH 2 ) 2 CO, is stored in the tank of a car. Calculate the mass, in kg, of the stored (NH 2 ) 2 CO. mass of (NH 2 ) 2 CO = .............................. kg [2]

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) Another oxide of nitrogen formed in car engines is nitrogen monoxide, NO. A catalytic converter removes NO by reacting it with a gas formed by incomplete combustion of the fuel. Two non‑toxic gases are formed.
